tasks.short: Set up, format and export publication-ready documents using desktop publishing software.

steps.what: Gather approved copy, images and production specifications from the {DOCS}.
Set page dimensions, styles and master pages in the {OTHER} publishing application.
Flow copy and graphics, then adjust pagination in the {OTHER} publishing application.
Check fonts, image resolution, overset text and bleed in the {OTHER} publishing application.
Export the proof and collect production files in the {OTHER} publishing application.

tasks.design: Configure reusable templates, import mappings and export presets in the {OTHER} publishing application. A small integration gathers approved versions from the {DOCS}, runs configured preflight checks and saves proofs with their source references. The publisher handles unusual pagination and composition; publication approval remains a separate action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates and preflight already exist, but variable source files and local production settings leave manual assembly between them.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing import and export features cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building narrow file adapters where scripting interfaces exist.
tasks.still_hard: Complex tables, unusual typography, missing fonts and print-specific requirements still need skilled intervention.
tasks.human_edge: The publisher judges whether a technically valid page communicates clearly and will reproduce well.

ambition.what: Template-based event flyers for internal event organisers.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from repeated setup and packaging towards difficult layouts and improving reusable templates. Publication decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Prepare event programmes from approved schedules.
reach.learn: Event information hierarchies, schedule changes and print deadlines.

evidence.claim: CHILI GraFx supports filling governed layout templates.
Configured styles, preflight profiles and export presets can reduce repetitive publishing operations.

assumptions: A recurring publication family has stable brand and production specifications.
The {OTHER} publishing application supports reusable templates and automated export.
Today's work is mainly screen-based; the prior's large meeting share is unlikely for this production task.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
The scope ends at proof handoff; external release requires its own approval.
Access work includes GDPR checks for personal content and consultation under national rules where applicable; no employee monitoring is proposed.
unknowns: Which publication formats recur most often?
Which scripting interfaces, licences and fonts are available?
How often do source files arrive without approval or usable production settings?
Which access and employee consultation requirements apply locally?
research_questions: Which required output formats can the publishing application's automation interface produce reliably?
Can representative complex tables and font substitutions pass the intended print specifications?
new_work: Maintain templates, import mappings and preflight profiles.
Resolve missing assets and failed exports.
Check representative outputs after software or font changes.

tasks.short: Arrange text and artwork into clear, visually appealing print or web pages.

steps.what: Find current copy and artwork in the {DOCS} and {CMS}.
Choose hierarchy, type scale and layout approach in the {OTHER} publishing application.
Position text and artwork within the chosen grid in the {OTHER} publishing application.
Judge reading order, balance and image crops in the {OTHER} publishing application.
Apply composition corrections and save the layout in the {OTHER} publishing application.

tasks.design: An integration presents approved content from the {DOCS} and {CMS} with stable asset references. Configured grids, styles and anchored elements in the {OTHER} publishing application handle repeat placement while the publisher chooses hierarchy and adjusts composition. Saved variants support early review without changing approved source copy.
tasks.previous_blocker: Content retrieval and routine placement are automatable, but useful composition depends on the particular message and audience.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable layout components and small content adapters make a constrained first layout practical. No new model capability is required.
tasks.still_hard: Novel page structures, editorial emphasis, culturally appropriate imagery and layouts across languages resist fixed rules.
tasks.human_edge: The publisher decides what readers should notice first and when breaking the grid improves comprehension.

ambition.what: Compare alternative reading orders before committing to a publication layout.

tasks.altitude: The publisher spends less time finding assets and repeating placement, leaving more time for composition alternatives. Creative decisions remain with the publisher; campaign approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Adapt publication hierarchy into responsive page layouts.
reach.learn: Responsive reflow, semantic reading order and keyboard-accessible content structure.

evidence.claim: CHILI GraFx provides governed template filling, supporting repeatable layout production.
Template placement can reduce mechanical work without resolving aesthetic hierarchy or audience fit.

assumptions: The work combines recurring page structures with some original composition.
Asset approval and usage rights are recorded upstream.
Screen work dominates this task; meetings occur mainly during brief clarification.
This task covers composition, overlapping with document production; its savings must not be added to that task's savings.
Build estimates cover one connected content collection and one publication family.
GDPR applies to personal content; any model use would also require applicable EU AI Act assessment.
Access estimates include consultation under national rules where required.
unknowns: What proportion of pages use established layouts?
Are asset versions and usage rights recorded consistently?
Does the publishing application support linked content and reusable components?
Which audiences and languages need distinct compositions?
research_questions: Can linked content preserve styles and asset references through revision?
Which layout constraints remain valid when copy expands across languages?
new_work: Maintain layout components and approved content mappings.
Repair broken content links and unsuitable automatic crops.
Review template changes against representative page types.

tasks.short: Check preliminary and final proofs, correct errors and record proof approval.

steps.what: Retrieve the current proof and approved source material from the {DOCS}.
Run spelling and technical checks in the {OTHER} publishing application.
Read the proof against approved copy and mark accepted corrections in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Proof text, approved copy, terminology rules and deterministic difference findings.
loop.output: Proposed corrections with page references, quoted evidence and reasons.
loop.check: Validate quoted spans and page references against source files. A publisher accepts or rejects each editorial correction.
loop.stop: One pass per section and one validation retry; enforce a document-size budget. Unreadable pages or unresolved findings return to manual proofing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Exact comparison finds changed text but cannot reliably distinguish an editorial error from an intentional variation.

steps.what: Apply accepted corrections in the {OTHER} publishing application.
Inspect the corrected proof for reflow and visual errors in the {OTHER} proof viewer.
Record proof approval or return outstanding issues through the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: Configured checks in the {OTHER} publishing application and deterministic source comparisons produce a page-linked issue list. A bounded model pass proposes contextual corrections, which the publisher approves before a script applies exact patches and regenerates the proof. The {PROJECT} records technical proof approval against the specific file version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Spelling and preflight checks cover mechanical errors, but contextual mistakes and corrections that alter pagination still require reading and visual inspection.
tasks.enabler_now: Text extraction, source comparison and narrowly scoped model review can assemble evidence for a reviewer. Existing publishing scripts can apply accepted changes where stable text anchors are available.
tasks.still_hard: Small visual defects, multilingual ambiguity, unsupported claims and text embedded in artwork can escape automated checks.
tasks.human_edge: The publisher assesses meaning, notices visual defects and recognises when a correction needs an editor or subject specialist.

ambition.what: Version comparison packs showing reviewers exactly what changed between proofs.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer repeated full-text comparisons and more contextual review and visual inspection. Technical proof approval remains with the publisher; editorial and campaign authority stay with their existing owners.

reach.task: Resolve recurring terminology and style inconsistencies across publications.
reach.learn: Editorial style decisions, source verification and escalation of substantive changes.

evidence.claim: Configured spelling checks and deterministic text comparisons can identify mechanical differences.
Bounded model review can propose contextual corrections, but visual and editorial approval still require people.

assumptions: Approved copy is available as a versioned reference.
Most proof text is extractable; image-only material follows an exception route.
The automation prior is moderated because contextual reading and final visual inspection remain substantial.
Automatic patches require a unique matching text anchor and a reversible change record.
Proof approval is distinct from permission to publish externally.
Build estimates cover one language and one publishing file format.
Personal or embargoed content requires controlled processing under GDPR; applicable EU AI Act duties depend on deployment.
Access estimates include consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Who owns technical, editorial and final publication approval?
Which languages and specialist terminology occur?
How often does copy exist only inside images or flattened proofs?
Can accepted changes be applied through a supported interface?
What processing environment is permitted for confidential content?
research_questions: How reliably can proof text be aligned to source text across columns and hyphenation?
What errors and false alarms occur on a representative reviewed proof set?
Can automated patches preserve typography and provide reliable rollback?
new_work: Review proposed contextual corrections and investigate ambiguous findings.
Maintain terminology rules and representative evaluation proofs.
Handle extraction failures and unmatched correction anchors.
Recheck visual output after automated edits.

tasks.short: Review work in progress, interpret feedback and modify layouts throughout production.

steps.what: Open the latest layout and inspect progress in the {OTHER} publishing application.
Read feedback in the {EMAIL} and assemble requested changes.

loop.input: Feedback messages, referenced proof versions and available page identifiers.
loop.output: Proposed change list with source quotes, target references and ambiguity flags.
loop.check: Require a source quote for every request and a valid version reference. The publisher confirms interpretation; ambiguous targets remain unresolved.
loop.stop: One extraction pass per feedback batch and one validation retry, within a fixed size budget. Unmapped comments return to manual triage.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text comments use implied references and combine several requests that fixed form fields cannot reliably recover.

steps.what: Discuss unclear or conflicting requests with the marketing manager.
Modify the layout to reflect resolved requests in the {OTHER} publishing application.
Compare revisions and record addressed comments in the {OTHER} proof review application.

tasks.design: Configure version-linked feedback and preview status in the {OTHER} proof review application, connected to the {PROJECT}. For feedback that still arrives through the {EMAIL}, a bounded extraction pass drafts a change list with source references. The publisher resolves conflicting requests, uses configured layout controls for routine edits and reviews deterministic revision comparisons before returning a proof.
tasks.previous_blocker: Feedback arrives against different versions and often uses vague language. Review tools can collect comments, but fragmented adoption leaves manual interpretation and reconciliation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing review features can handle structured comments, while a bounded extraction loop helps with residual free-text messages. Small integrations can connect comment status to specific proof versions.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting stakeholder intent, late scope changes and visual feedback without clear targets need discussion and skilled editing.
tasks.human_edge: The publisher translates stakeholder intent into a coherent page and explains the consequences of competing requests.

ambition.what: Resolve scope and feedback conflicts at each review round before layout changes begin.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from locating comments and checking versions towards resolving intent and making visual changes. Existing escalation and publication rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Assess the production impact of late campaign changes.
reach.learn: Campaign priorities, approval ownership and trade-offs between scope and publication deadlines.

evidence.claim: Version-linked comments and revision comparisons can reduce feedback reconciliation work.
A bounded model can extract proposed changes from free text while leaving ambiguous intent to a person.

assumptions: Feedback commonly mixes structured proof comments with messages.
Configured review forms replace message extraction wherever reviewers adopt them.
The prior's mailbox share is increased here because this task explicitly includes interpreting instructions and feedback.
Human discussion remains necessary only where requests are unclear or conflict.
Internal revisions are reversible drafts; external release sits outside this task.
Editing and comparison overlap with the other listed tasks; savings are not additive.
Access is restricted to publication feedback, with GDPR retention controls and applicable EU AI Act assessment for model processing.
Consultation under national rules is included where required; no individual productivity tracking is proposed.
unknowns: Where do reviewers currently leave comments?
Who can resolve conflicting requests and accept scope changes?
Can the review application export comment status and revision references?
What mailbox access and retention limits apply?
research_questions: Can feedback references be preserved when pages move or proofs are regenerated?
How reliably does extraction distinguish requests, suggestions and withdrawn comments?
Which comment export interfaces support dependable version reconciliation?
new_work: Confirm extracted requests and resolve ambiguous targets.
Maintain version mappings and reviewer access.
Handle comments submitted against obsolete proofs.
Monitor extraction quality and update the bounded prompt when recurring failures appear.

role.altitude: The publisher spends less time assembling files, repeating formatting and reconciling comments. More time goes to visual hierarchy, difficult production cases and editorial coordination; final publication authority changes only through explicit organisational delegation.
reach: Help event planners produce dependable programmes from approved schedules.
Work with editors on terminology and evidence-backed corrections.
Help web and digital interface designers preserve reading order across formats.
Give marketing managers clearer production consequences for late changes.
skills_to_grow: Content schemas, asset metadata and version control.
Print preflight and accessible document structure.
Evaluation of model-proposed corrections against source evidence.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a governed publication service that lets adjacent teams prepare routine materials from approved content, while the publisher concentrates on composition, exceptions and production quality.
